sentences.text: Shri K.N. Gupta, learned Senior Counsel with Shri Harshad Bahirani, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Pratip Visoriya, learned Government Advocate for the respondents/State.

Challenge is to an order dated 08/03/2019 passed in Writ Petition No.2129/2017; whereby, the challenge to order dated 17/01/2017 passed by the District Supply Officer, Gwalior, cancelling the allotment of fair price shop No.161 Code No. 405120 has been negatived.
The cancellation of allotment of fair price shop was on the findings of irregularities committed by the society in the distribution of essential commodities.
The cancellation was questioned on merit as well as the propriety.

sentences.text: As to propriety, it was the contention by the appellant that it was beyond jurisdiction of the District Supply Officer to have straight away cancelled the shop without first cancelling the fair price shop allotment authority letter.
The contentions were negatived.
Learned single Judge observed:-

"Pertinently the term allotment letter does not find mention in the definition clause of 2015, Control Order. Clause-8 relates to allotment of fair price shops to the THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. State of M.P. and others extent that Fair Price Shop Allotment Authority shall allot fair price shops only to such societies/groups as recognized by Scheduled-2 of 2015, Control Order.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. State of M.P. and others
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thus, the formal mode of allotment of fair price shop is by issuance of fair price shop allotment authority letter as defined under the Clause-2 (k) of 2015, Control Order.
The impugned order Annexure P-2 has cancelled the said allotment letter.
This is not a case that the work of fair price shop was attached without suspending the letter of authority.

It is contended that learned Single Judge miscontrued the provisions contained in Control Order 16 of Control Order 2015 whereunder unless the fair price shop Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82559072/

sentences.text: Control Order 8 lays down the procedure for allotment of fair price shops.
Clause (3) of Control Order 8 provides that, eligible institutions, interested in operation of fair price shop shall apply to the fair price shop allotment authority prescribed in Form-A.
That the fair price shop allotment authority issues letter in prescribed Form-B which entitles the concerned institution to operate fair price shops as per clause 10 of the Control Order.

Furthermore,
clauses 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 of Control Order make provision regarding distribution;
allocation, storage & transportation; prevention of substitution, diversion &
adulteration; inspection and supervision and the power to enter, search and seize,
respectively.

Control order 16, which we are presently concerned with, envisages:-
"16. Punishment and Penalty.-

(1) In case of contravention of any provision of Central / State order or this order, the fair price shop authority letter may be suspended or cancelled and security amount may be forfeited wholly or partially by shop allotment authority.
In such case, forfeited amount shall be recoverable from guilty employee of concerning institution.

(2) In case of violation under clause 13 for quantity more than 10 percent of the monthly allocation or repetition of violation under the same clause, a person shall mandatorily be prosecuted under section 7 of Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (No.

2 (4) Fair price shop allotment authority, after giving reasonable opportunity to fair price shop to submit its representation in writing and following principle of natural justice, may cancel authority letter mentioning the reason thereof:
Provided that, Fair price shop allotment authority shall not allot that fair price shop to any new society/institution till the final disposal of the appeal.

(5) During suspension/ cancellation of a fair price shop, Fair price shop allotment authority shall make alternative arrangement from a nearby fair price shop to ensure distribution of commodities to card holders attached with such shop:
Provided that, a fair price shop of rural area shall not be attached with a fair price shop in urban area and vice-versa.

(6) If any essential commodity is diverted or distributed to any ineligible person by authorised agency/ fair price shop owner, the price thereof shall be recovered, from responsible salesperson/ employee/ person at the rate of prevailing market price or economic cost (after reducing cost price), whichever is higher.
Such amount shall be recoverable as an arrear of land revenue.

(7) Shop allotment authority may order, in writing, to institution to remove the salesperson of fair price shop, if found guilty, from duties of distribution of commodities of Public Distribution System.
Such order shall be binding on institution and the said salesperson shall not be appointed as salesperson in any other fair price shop.

(8) On finding an irregularity in operation of a fair price shop, if it is expedient in the opinion of the Collector, prosecution against chairman or head of the society/
salesperson/ employee of institution may be initiated.

(9) If any action has been contemplated under the provisions of this order or Co-operative Act against THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. The expressions "Fair Price Shop", "Fair Price Shop Allotment Authority", "Fair Price Shop Allotment Authority Letter" find their meaning in Control Order 2(i) (j) (k) reproduced herebelow:-
"(i) "Fair Price Shop" means shop which has been issued authority letter under this order to distribute essential commodities to ration card holders under Targeted Public Distribution System.

(j) "Fair Price Shop Allotment Authority" means District Supply Controller or District Supply Officer for urban area of the District headquarters and Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) of concerned Sub-Division for remaining areas of the district.

(k) "Fair Price Shop Allotment Authority Letter" means an authority letter issued by Fair Price Shop Allotment Authority in favour of an institution to operate fair price shop as per the provisions of this control order."
Evidently, unless the fair price shop allotment authority issues a letter in Form-B, an institution/society cannot run a fair price shop.
Close reading of Form-'B' reveals that it is an authority given for running a fair price shop with various conditions stipulated therein.
Thus it is magna carta for the operation of fair price shop.

Control Order 16 empowers the fair price shop allotment authority to suspend or cancel and forfeit security amount wholly or partially in case of contravention of any provision of Central/ State THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. State of M.P. and others order or Control Order, 2015.

sentences.text: In case of suspension of a fair price shop, the fair price shop allotment authority is under obligation to issue show cause notice to concerned fair price shop within ten days and pass final order within three months.
The fair price shop allotment authority can also cancel authority letter after giving reasonable opportunity to fair price shop to submit its representation in writing.
It is further borne out that in case of cancellation of authority letter, the fair price shop cannot allotted to any new society/ institution till final disposal of the appeal.

However, in case of suspension/ cancellation of fair price shop, it is within the competence of fair price shop allotment authority to make alternate arrangement from a nearby fair price shop to ensure distribution of commodities to card holders attached to such shop.

In other words, in case of suspension/
cancellation of fair price shop authority letter, such authority cannot be allotted to any new society/
institution till final disposal of the appeal.

Whereas, in case fair price shop is suspended or canceled,
the allotment authority can make alternate arrangement from nearby fair price shop to ensure distribution of commodities to card holders attached to such shop.

Bare reading of Control Order 16 makes it clear that there are two prone actions that fair price shop authority can take under Control THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. State of M.P. and others Order 16, i.e.,
suspension or cancellation of fair price shop allotment letter or suspension or cancellation of fair price shop.

In other words, though the fair price shop authority letter has not been canceled but the shop allotted on the basis thereof has been canceled for the irregularity committed by the allottee.

sentences.text: The said contention, therefore, fails.
As regard to merit, trite it is that in exercise of jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, it is the decision making process which can be interfered with and not on merit.

In the case at hand, the District Supply Officer as well as the Appellate Authority having found the complaint of irregularity/ illegality committed by the appellant - society, established in an enquiry wherein the appellant was afforded an opportunity of hearing, we do not perceive any error of judgment arrived at by learned Single Judge in declining to cause any indulgence on merit.
Taking any view of the matter, the appeal being devoid of merit is dismissed.
No costs.
(Sanjay Yadav) (Vivek Agarwal)

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Evidently, unless the fair price shop allotment authority issues a letter in Form-B, an institution/society cannot run a fair price shop.
Close reading of Form-'B' reveals that it is an authority given for running a fair price shop with various conditions stipulated therein.
Thus it is magna carta for the operation of fair price shop.
Control Order 16 empowers the fair price shop allotment authority to suspend or cancel and forfeit security amount wholly or partially in case of contravention of any provision of Central/ State THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. State of M.P. and others order or Control Order, 2015.
In case of suspension of a fair price shop, the fair price shop allotment authority is under obligation to issue show cause notice to concerned fair price shop within ten days and pass final order within three months.
The fair price shop allotment authority can also cancel authority letter after giving reasonable opportunity to fair price shop to submit its representation in writing.
However, in case of suspension/ cancellation of fair price shop, it is within the competence of fair price shop allotment authority to make alternate arrangement from a nearby fair price shop to ensure distribution of commodities to card holders attached to such shop.
In other words, in case of suspension/
cancellation of fair price shop authority letter, such authority cannot be allotted to any new society/
institution till final disposal of the appeal.
Whereas, in case fair price shop is suspended or canceled,
the allotment authority can make alternate arrangement from nearby fair price shop to ensure distribution of commodities to card holders attached to such shop.
Bare reading of Control Order 16 makes it clear that there are two prone actions that fair price shop authority can take under Control THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. State of M.P. and others Order 16, i.e.,
suspension or cancellation of fair price shop allotment letter or suspension or cancellation of fair price shop.
In other words, though the fair price shop authority letter has not been canceled but the shop allotted on the basis thereof has been canceled for the irregularity committed by the allottee.
Thus, it cannot be said that the fair price shop authority acted without jurisdiction.
Furthermore, making of alternate arrangement, in our considered opinion, will not invalidate the order of cancellation of fair price shop.
In view whereof, the exercise of the power by District Supply Officer in canceling the shop allotted to the appellant cannot be found to be beyond jurisdiction as is being contended on behalf of the THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH Manisha Mahila Prathmik Upbhokta Sahakari Bhandar Maryadit Vs. State of M.P. and others appellant.
As regard to merit, trite it is that in exercise of jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, it is the decision making process which can be interfered with and not on merit.
In the case at hand, the District Supply Officer as well as the Appellate Authority having found the complaint of irregularity/ illegality committed by the appellant - society, established in an enquiry wherein the appellant was afforded an opportunity of hearing, we do not perceive any error of judgment arrived at by learned Single Judge in declining to cause any indulgence on merit.
